title: Older New Orleans pianists
summary: He recalls an uncle, Walter Lewis and Papa French.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Yeah. But he comes out of that same, that same period, yeah. Same period, same thing? Yeah, because I had another uncle, Uncle Tat, his brother, they called him Summer Ross, and he could play, man. They had several guys around there, man, those guys could play, man. And when you heard them you had to sit down and listen. Whatever you were doing you just sit down and take note of what's going on. Oh yeah. Oh yeah. Yeah. Yeah, like Walter Lewis, man. Walter, about in his eighties, man. And Walter as quiet as Walter can really play the piano when you want. If you just sit down and just let him play. Because he went on the road by himself. He had a booking agency. He used to take them all across the country playing. And then later on he came back, he played with Placidi, he played with Papa French, and he played with different ones. I played with Papa French a couple of times, and I played with different ones.

I've never heard him play blues. He's always played more, I don't know, supper music. Whenever I hear him, I'm going, wait a minute, man. Can we do something a little more raunchy? Come on. Yeah. And he's always in a situation where he's got to play. Yeah. Like, you know, he's got to play to the audience, so to speak.
That's right. But, was that a lot, did that happen? Did you ever have to like play to the audience? You know what I'm saying?
